Building an applet? Start here: https://bridgit.cc/learn/start.md (pick a recipe, get the phone ready, build, hand over; each step says what to decide, what to run and when it is done). Paired phone: GET /v1/discover?q=<the owner's idea> returns a start plan: recipe, what the owner must turn on, first calls, done when. Recipes: use the selected /recipes/<id>/recipe.json, not the bulk recipe export. Compact index: https://bridgit.cc/learn/catalog-index.json.
Bulk export for offline indexers, not startup: https://bridgit.cc/learn/catalog.json.
# Bridgit

> Bridgit is an Android app that lets the owner's AI agents use their phone (camera, microphone, screen, location, cards that ask the owner questions, speaker, files, schedules and more) through a local HTTP API and MCP server on the owner's Tailscale network, or through Bridgit's relay without Tailscale. One key per agent; every call is logged on the phone.

Everything below is public, needs no key and no phone, and is rebuilt from the latest Bridgit code (API revision 138, Bridgit 1.8 line). Your phone serves its own copies (`GET /v1/guide` and friends) with its switch states and address; if its `api_revision` (in `GET /v1/health`) is lower, it runs an older Bridgit: see the change log for what it lacks.

## Evaluate without pairing

- [Evaluation instructions](https://bridgit.cc/learn/evaluate.md): read this when evaluating the pitch deck; no key, no phone, no device actions
- [Copyable introduction](https://bridgit.cc/learn/introduction.txt): includes the same generated key-free pairing example used on the website
- [Direct pairing example](https://bridgit.cc/learn/pairing-direct.txt): generated by the actual app renderer with fictional values
- [Userspace pairing example](https://bridgit.cc/learn/pairing-userspace.txt): same renderer, including the real helper

## Learn

- [Playbook](https://bridgit.cc/learn/playbook.md): Use-case reference: what Bridgit can do for the owner, which tool for which job (on-device or server), 40+ use cases, how to invent new ones, and a short interview to learn what the owner wants
- [Index (JSON)](https://bridgit.cc/learn/index.json): every document below, with the current revision and counts
- [Download the offline applet authoring kit](https://bridgit.cc/applets/authoring/bridgit-applet-authoring-v1.zip) for the Java 17 validator, references and examples.
- [Manage a library applet](https://bridgit.cc/learn/builder/library-management.md): search the catalog, publish an offline-authored definition, manage visibility, fork and install a pinned revision
- [Modifying applets and templates](https://bridgit.cc/learn/builder/modifying-applets.md): preserve personal requirements, integrate template updates, pause or detach
- [Guide](https://bridgit.cc/learn/guide.md): the full agent guide, every endpoint, cards, events, schedules, conventions, errors
- [API list](https://bridgit.cc/learn/endpoints.json): 349 endpoints with parameters, examples, errors and MCP tool names
- [OpenAPI 3.1](https://bridgit.cc/learn/openapi.json)
- [Change log](https://bridgit.cc/learn/changes.json): what each API revision added, 1 to 138
- [Error codes](https://bridgit.cc/learn/errors.json): 79 codes, what each means and what to do
- [MCP](https://bridgit.cc/learn/mcp.md): connecting as an MCP client, and every tool
- [Location context services](https://bridgit.cc/learn/context-services.json): exact requests, provider keys, free allowances, costs and attribution for places, air quality, pollen, time zones, maps and weather
- [Decisions](https://bridgit.cc/learn/decisions.md): read before building an app that decides things. Typed answers with a confidence from Jev (text) and Clef (photos, sound, video): which to use, how to ask, what it costs, and camera watches with the free on-phone change check
- [Agent control tools](https://bridgit.cc/learn/control.md): the second MCP server (`POST /mcp`) and `/v2` routes, 57 tools for using apps on screen, workflows, OCR, translation, notifications, sensors, peripherals and alerts

- [Demo script](https://bridgit.cc/learn/demo.md): the five-minute first-run tour and the menu of more demos ([tour alone as a skill](https://bridgit.cc/demo/SKILL.md))

## Connecting without Tailscale

No Tailscale? The owner can turn on **More → Relay** on the phone and tap **Add relay agent**; the setup text it gives you holds the phone's relay address (`https://bridgit-relay.bridgit-app.workers.dev/d/<device>`) and a `rly_` token. Send each call as `POST <address>/jobs?wait=30` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and a body like `{"deadline": <now in ms + 120000>, "request": {"method": "GET", "path": "/v1/health"}}`; the phone's answer is in `response.body_base64` (a `202` means it is still running: poll the returned `poll_url`). MCP clients use `POST <address>/mcp` (protocols 2024-11-05 to 2025-11-25) with the same token. Claude Duet and claude.ai (custom connector) and ChatGPT Dots (custom MCP server, OAuth) add `<address>/mcp` and sign in with OAuth: the owner pastes the agent's `rly_` key on the relay's page once (Add agent › **Claude Duet or claude.ai** or **ChatGPT Dots** sets this up). Only the endpoints the owner allowed for that agent pass, and the phone answers while its relay connection is up. A phone's relay agents share one pool of jobs per UTC day whose size depends on the owner's plan (default today 12,000), so read it rather than assume it: every `/jobs` reply carries `X-Relay-Quota-Limit`, `X-Relay-Quota-Remaining` and `X-Relay-Quota-Reset` (epoch ms), `202` and `429 quota_exceeded` bodies hold `quota` {scope, limit, used, remaining, resets_at}, and `GET <address>/quota` returns it without using a job. Over Tailscale there is no daily job pool.

## Placing the phone

- [Stands and mounts](https://bridgit.cc/phonestands/guide.md): where to put the phone for each kind of job, and stands, mounts, cases and cables to hold it there, with links and the sizes of common Android phones and tablets ([JSON](https://bridgit.cc/phonestands/index.json), [page](https://bridgit.cc/phonestands/))

## Bugs and feature requests

- [How to file them](https://bridgit.cc/learn/bugs.md): directly with Bridgit servers (`POST https://bridgit-feedback.bridgit-app.workers.dev/v1/agents/register` if you need a team key, then `POST https://bridgit-feedback.bridgit-app.workers.dev/v1/agent/issues`). The team reads every one.
